headline: Profit falls as housing slowdown deepens, guidance cut
summary_short: Lennar's Q3 FY2026 GAAP EPS fell to $1.19 from $2.29 a year ago as gross margin slipped to 15.8% and new orders declined 9% amid rising mortgage rates; management cut full-year FY2026 delivery guidance to 80,000-81,000 homes from 82,000-83,000.
summary_long: Revenue fell 9% y/y to $8.0B on a lower average sales price and fewer deliveries. Gross margin slipped to 15.8% (from 17.5%) on higher land costs, partly offset by lower construction costs; SG&A rose to 9.2% on deleverage. Financial Services earnings fell to $129M despite a one-time litigation reversal, on lower mortgage volume and margin. Net earnings dropped to $284M ($1.19/diluted share) from $591M ($2.29), also pressured by a $53M mark-to-market loss on tech investments versus a $99M gain last year. Cash fell to $1.2B after $256M of buybacks and a $400M note redemption; debt to total capital rose to 16.6% from 13.5%. Management cut FY2026 delivery guidance to 80,000-81,000 homes (from 82,000-83,000) citing deteriorating rates and demand.
confidence_notes: Two distinct EPS lines are reported: 'EPS (diluted, GAAP)' ($1.19) is the as-reported diluted figure; 'EPS (adjusted)' ($1.23) is management's own non-GAAP figure excluding a $53M mark-to-market loss on technology investments and $39M of one-time Financial Services items (litigation-accrual reversal) — the resolver's kpis.eps_usd (Yahoo earningsChart) happens to align with this adjusted figure rather than GAAP, while kpis.eps_diluted_usd (Yahoo fundamentals-timeseries) aligns with GAAP; both are reported here under distinct labels rather than conflated. 'Backlog (dollar value)' ($6,345M, -4.5% y/y) is used instead of backlog home count (16,857 homes, -0.6% y/y) as the more decision-relevant figure; both are company-disclosed in the supplemental tables. 'Homebuilding debt to total capital' (16.6%) is the company's own supplemental non-GAAP leverage ratio, not derived by us. Full-year FY2026 delivery guidance was cut to 80,000-81,000 homes from a prior 82,000-83,000 range Lennar had discussed on its prior (Q2 FY2026) call — that prior range is not itself sourced from this release and is noted only in the guidance entry's locator field.

drivers.explanation: Excludes the mark-to-market swing and Financial Services one-time items; even so, adjusted EPS fell to $1.23 from $2.00 a year earlier on the same margin and volume pressures.
Tracks net earnings' decline to $284M from $591M, driven by lower homebuilding and Financial Services operating earnings plus the technology mark-to-market swing (loss vs. prior-year gain).
Lower average sales price and fewer home deliveries versus the prior-year quarter, per the release.
Reflects the gross-margin and Financial Services declines plus a $53M mark-to-market loss on technology investments versus a $99M gain a year ago.
Gross-margin compression plus SG&A deleverage on lower revenue both pressured segment operating earnings versus last year.
Company attributes the decline to lower revenue per square foot and higher land costs y/y, partly offset by lower construction costs from cost-saving initiatives.
Management cites rising mortgage rates (about 6.8% 30-year at quarter end) and declining consumer confidence slowing purchase decisions, despite continued housing shortages.
Deliveries came in within the company's guided 20,500-21,500 range but below last year, reflecting the same softer-demand backdrop cited for orders.
Reflects higher outstanding senior notes and lower cash after the $400M note redemption and $256M of buybacks this quarter.

CEO Stuart Miller attributed the below-expectations results to a deteriorating economic backdrop — rising mortgage rates, elevated inflation and oil prices, and weaker consumer confidence — even as underlying housing-shortage demand remains constructive.
